corrections.field_01: Strongest feature: The reply differentiates Platonist objectivity and necessary existence from conceptualist intrinsic mentality, then presents divine conceptualism as a unified explanatory architecture responsive to both theoretical motivations. Principal limitation: It identifies a conjunction of desiderata without independently establishing that primitive nonmental intentionality cannot secure comparable objectivity, necessity, and representational directedness, or that theological supplementation improves economy. Live burden: The comparative case therefore depends on demonstrating why mentality explains propositional intentionality more satisfactorily than Platonist primitiveness, while showing that human conceptualism’s shortcomings do not exhaust the available alternatives. Locked score: The assessment appropriately reflects a highly relevant, explicitly qualified, substantially responsive synthesis whose conceptual organization exceeds its comparatively underdeveloped defense of exclusivity, necessity, and theoretical advantage.
